title: Elliptic: Anti-Money Laundering in Bitcoin
finding: Compares tabular and graph classifiers on a Bitcoin transaction graph; Random Forest was strongest in the reported comparison.
implication: Benchmark simple supervised models before introducing GNN complexity.
limit: Crypto transaction labels do not validate bank-account or beneficial-owner decisions.

title: Realistic Synthetic Financial Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering Models
finding: Introduces a synthetic transaction generator and public AML benchmarks.
implication: Use synthetic bank-like transaction data for controlled experiments and typology coverage.
limit: Synthetic labels reflect simulator assumptions; performance does not establish operational efficacy.

title: The Shape of Money Laundering: Elliptic2
finding: Frames suspicious activity as classification of connected subgraphs rather than isolated nodes.
implication: Evaluate case-level subgraphs alongside transaction-level predictions.
limit: Requires candidate generation and substantial graph infrastructure; crypto evidence is not banking validation.

title: A synthetic data set to benchmark anti-money laundering methods
finding: Presents synthetic AML data for comparing statistical and machine learning approaches.
implication: Add an independent synthetic benchmark instead of relying on one generator.
limit: Inspect the actual schema and labels before selecting graph or ownership tasks.

title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
finding: Learns neighborhood aggregation functions that generalize to unseen nodes.
implication: Consider sampled inductive models for newly opened accounts.
limit: Inductive capacity does not solve temporal leakage or missing customer context.

title: Modeling Relational Data with Graph Convolutional Networks
finding: Uses relation-specific message passing for multi-relational graphs.
implication: Preserve transaction, ownership, and identity edge types in experimental models.
limit: Knowledge-base completion scores cannot be treated as verified registry facts.

title: Graph Attention Networks
finding: Uses masked attention to learn different weights over neighbors.
implication: Include a weighted-neighbor model in a bounded experimental comparison.
limit: Attention weights are not proof of causality or a complete explanation.

title: EvolveGCN: Evolving Graph Convolutional Networks for Dynamic Graphs
finding: Evolves graph convolution parameters across changing graph snapshots.
implication: Test snapshot-based modeling if graph structure shifts over time.
limit: Snapshot resolution can hide transaction ordering and rapid pass-through behavior.

title: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs
finding: Combines temporal event processing, graph operators, and node memory.
implication: Consider event-time models after establishing a causal snapshot baseline.
limit: Memory updates, delayed events, and replay semantics add operational complexity.

title: GNNExplainer: Generating Explanations for Graph Neural Networks
finding: Identifies compact subgraphs and feature subsets important to a prediction.
implication: Evaluate explanation fidelity and stability against source-backed graph paths.
limit: A model explanation is neither causal attribution nor legal evidence by itself.

title: Enhancing Graph Neural Network-based Fraud Detectors against Camouflaged Fraudsters
finding: Studies feature and relation camouflage and selective neighborhood aggregation.
implication: Stress-test dilution of risky neighborhoods by benign-looking neighbors.
limit: Fraud benchmark outcomes do not automatically transfer to AML investigations.

title: xFraud: Explainable Fraud Transaction Detection
finding: Combines heterogeneous transaction detection with an explanation component.
implication: Separate the risk detector from an independently inspectable evidence view.
limit: Fraud and money laundering have different labels, loss functions, and analyst objectives.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
finding: Combines a parametric generator with explicit retrieved memory.
implication: Retrieve approved source excerpts and resolve citations before drafting narratives.
limit: Retrieval does not guarantee that generated claims are entailed by sources.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
finding: Interleaves model-driven reasoning and actions in interactive tasks.
implication: Use bounded read-only tools and an explicit investigation state machine.
limit: Interactive benchmark success does not justify autonomous compliance decisions.

title: LaundroGraph: Self-Supervised Graph Representation Learning for Anti-Money Laundering
finding: Learns customer and transaction representations from a banking graph through link prediction.
implication: Test behavioral embeddings with a separate assessment of analyst usefulness.
limit: Its private banking data and proxy objective limit direct reproduction.

title: Provably Powerful Graph Neural Networks for Directed Multigraphs
finding: Studies adaptations including direction and port numbering for multigraph expressivity.
implication: Retain directed parallel transfers when selecting graph operators.
limit: FinGraph implements a simpler directed GraphSAGE comparator without port numbering.

title: Graph Feature Preprocessor: Real-time Subgraph-based Feature Extraction for Financial Crime Detection
finding: Extracts temporal graph motifs and account statistics for tree models. The authors compare basic and enriched features on chronological holdouts.
implication: Test graph features with boosting first and match feature visibility to the decision time.
limit: Batch size changes how much context is visible. Published F1 and throughput apply to that benchmark and deployment setting.

title: FlowScope: Spotting Money Laundering Based on Graphs
finding: Uses flow structure across multipartite graphs to detect suspicious chains.
implication: Measure amounts and temporal ordering in addition to graph connectivity.
limit: A detected pattern still needs economic context and source verification.

title: Towards Collaborative Anti-Money Laundering Among Financial Institutions
finding: Studies collaborative scatter-gather discovery under separated institutional graphs.
implication: Evaluate missing cross-bank edges as a source of detection failure.
limit: Federated sharing needs an explicit privacy model and institutional governance.

title: Temporal Graph Benchmark for Machine Learning on Temporal Graphs
finding: Provides temporal graph tasks and reproducible evaluation protocols.
implication: Keep event-time splits and graph visibility explicit.
limit: Results on temporal link prediction do not measure AML classification.

title: Towards Better Evaluation for Dynamic Link Prediction
finding: Shows the effect of evaluation choices and negative sampling on dynamic prediction.
implication: Record the negative population and time boundary of every experiment.
limit: FinGraph uses observed transaction labels rather than sampled link negatives.

title: Knowledge Graphs
finding: Surveys graph representation, querying, reasoning, quality, and applications.
implication: Assign distinct roles to the asserted graph, validation rules, and learned features.
limit: A broad survey supplies architectural guidance rather than a financial-crime benchmark.

title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
finding: Examines confidence miscalibration and post-hoc calibration methods.
implication: Evaluate reliability on a dedicated temporal calibration set before interpreting scores as probabilities.
limit: The present experiment has no fitted calibration stage.

title: The precision-recall plot is more informative than the ROC plot when evaluating binary classifiers on imbalanced datasets
finding: Examines precision-recall evaluation under class imbalance.
implication: Report average precision, prevalence, and review-budget metrics together.
limit: Metrics vary with prevalence and the selected alert population.

title: Parameterized Explainer for Graph Neural Network
finding: Learns a parameterized generator for graph explanations across instances.
implication: Assess explanation fidelity and stability before integrating an explainer.
limit: Explainer outputs require separate evidence provenance and analyst interpretation.

title: (Almost) All of Entity Resolution
finding: Reviews probabilistic linkage, clustering, and canonicalization.
implication: Track candidate identity matches, provenance, and reversible merge decisions.
limit: The implementation requires resolved source identifiers and does not automate fuzzy merges.
